subject: Request: Nightly batch latency bridge for reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Sujan Patel <sujan@gridline.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@gridline.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 21:12:00 -0400
Subject: Nightly batch window causing tail latency spikes — request for temporary SLA tweak

Hi Kimberly,

Quick note from Gridline's ops team: our nightly bulk-embedding job (runs 02:00–04:00 UTC) has been causing repeated tail-latency spikes against our Dedicated pool. Since these are large, long-running batches they push concurrency beyond our reserved token-level assumptions and we saw 95th/99th percentile tails breach our SLAs on 2027-09-22 and 2027-09-23.

We attached the operation log with a couple of representative traces (operation-log-2027-09-22.csv). Can Redwood provision a temporary "latency bridge" for these windows so we don’t get hit with SLA credits while we implement a sharded-workload approach? Specifically, we are asking for:

- A soft carveout from 02:00–04:00 UTC for two weeks to allow higher inflight concurrency for our nightly jobs,
- A guaranteed preemption policy so interactive traffic keeps priority,
- Reduced penalty/crediting during the carveout (or a path to credits forgiveness).

We understand this is an exception; we’re happy to accept a short-term commercial addendum while we refactor. I can loop in procurement/legal if helpful.

Can you confirm what information you need to evaluate and whether a 2-week canary is workable?

Thanks,
Sujan Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Gridline AI
S: +1-415-555-0172

--- Attachment: operation-log-2027-09-22.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Sujan Patel <sujan@gridline.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly batch window causing tail latency spikes — request for temporary SLA tweak

Hi Sujan — thanks for the detail and for the logs. I copied Ben and Lauren to confirm commercial and operational commitments. A few quick items/questions before we scope a formal addendum: 

- Can you share the typical request concurrency and avg token/sec during the batch window (sample histograms would help)?
- Are the jobs always scheduled in a tight window (02:00–04:00 UTC) or do you have variable starts?
- What rollback conditions would you want if the carveout impacts interactive latency beyond agreed thresholds?

Operationally, our proposed interim approach (two-week canary) would look like this:

1) Nightly buffer: Reserve a small burst pool (6 GPUs equivalent) for 02:00–04:00 UTC dedicated to Gridline batch jobs.
2) Soft preemption: Interactive requests continue to get prioritized; batch tokens are preemptable but we will only preempt down to a safe baseline (will provide exact token preemption thresholds).
3) Observability: We’ll provide token-level latency dashboards and a shared alerting threshold for immediate rollback.
4) Credit policy: For the canary period we propose a temporary carveout from SLA crediting — we will not issue credit for any breach attributable to this scheduled buffer, provided Gridline adheres to agreed concurrency caps.

I attached a draft of the operational config we’d apply for the canary (proposed-bridge-config.yaml).

If that sounds acceptable we can do a 30-minute call Monday to finalize the config and Ben can sketch the commercial addendum. What time works on your side?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: proposed-bridge-config.yaml (YAML, stub)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sujan Patel <sujan@gridline.ai>; kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Sep 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly batch window causing tail latency spikes — request for temporary SLA tweak

Sujan — thanks for raising this and Kim for the clear runbook. Commercial points from our side: 

- For a temporary nightly buffer we typically bill an interim fee tied to reserved GPU-hour equivalence. For the 02:00–04:00 UTC window, a conservative estimate is 6 GPU equivalents × 2 hours × nightly run days. If Gridline opts into a 12-month commitment to maintain the buffer, we can offer a 15% discount on the addendum fee.
- Draft amendment: I’m attaching a skeleton (draft-amendment-nightly-buffer.docx) that describes the term (2-week canary, auto-convert to a monthly addendum unless terminated), the credit carveout language, and the rollback triggers.
- Observability & credits: We’ll include token/route SLO dashboards and clear rules for attribution. Credits will not be issued for breaches directly attributable to the scheduled buffer, but we will define an emergency rollback credit formula if interactive latency exceeds agreed thresholds more than 3 times in 48 hours.

If useful I can propose specific numbers for the fee and run a quick ROI calc for you. I’m available Monday 10:00–12:00 PDT for the config + commercial sync.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: draft-amendment-nightly-buffer.docx (DOCX, stub)

From: Sujan Patel <sujan@gridline.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@gridline.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly batch window causing tail latency spikes — request for temporary SLA tweak

Kim, Ben — appreciate the quick turn. The proposal looks workable and a two-week canary is acceptable from Gridline's side. A couple of clarifications before we lock the call: 

- Rollback policy: We want a documented rollback sequence and a 30-minute emergency contact window (phone/Slack) if interactive latency degrades.
- Attribution: We’ll provide an initial concurrency histogram by EOD Sunday so you can finalize thresholds.
- Legal: procurement/legal will review the draft amendment; please include a definition of "attributable breach" and a list of metrics used for attribution.

Monday 10:30 PDT works for Gridline for the operations + commercial sync. Please share a short agenda (30 min). Once we sign the canary addendum we’ll schedule the first night deploy for Tuesday 02:00 UTC.

Thanks,
Sujan
Head of Infrastructure, Gridline AI
Phone: +1-415-555-0172
